messages.content: What is the total circumference of four circles, where the first circle has a radius of 5cm, the second circle has a radius of 10cm, the third circle has a radius of 15cm, and the fourth circle has a radius of 20cm?

function.name: calculate_circumference
function.description: Calculates the circumference of a circle with a given radius. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

radius.description: The radius of the circle in the unit given.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the radius. Default is m.

message.content:
The circumference \(C\) of a single circle is  

\[
C \;=\; 2\,\pi r .
\]

For each of your circles we have:

| Circle | Radius \(r\) | Circumference \(C = 2\pi r\) |
|--------|--------------|-------------------------------|
| 1      | 5 cm         | \(2\pi(5)=10\pi\;\text{cm}\)   |
| 2      | 10 cm        | \(2\pi(10)=20\pi\;\text{cm}\)  |
| 3      | 15 cm        | \(2\pi(15)=30\pi\;\text{cm}\)  |
| 4      | 20 cm        | \(2\pi(20)=40\pi\;\text{cm}\)  |

Adding them together gives the **total** circumference:

\[
\begin{aligned}
C_{\text{tot}} &= 10\pi + 20\pi + 30\pi + 40\pi \\[4pt]
               &= (10+20+30+40)\,\pi \\[4pt]
               &= 100\,\pi \;\text{cm}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Numerically,

\[
C_{\text{tot}}\approx 100\times 3.14159 \approx 314.16\;\text{cm}.
\]

So the combined perimeter length around all four circles equals **\(100\pi\) centimeters**, which is about **314.16 cm**.
message.reasoning:
We need sum of circumferences. Use formula C=2πr. Radii cm. Compute each:

C1=2π*5=10π ≈31.4159 cm.

C2=2π*10=20π≈62.8318 cm.

C3=30π≈94.2477 cm.

C4=40π≈125.6637 cm.

Sum= (10+20+30+40)π=100π≈314.159265 cm.

Thus answer ~314.16 cm or exactly 100π cm. Provide explanation. No tool needed.
